summary: The seaward light of Victoria Harbour's Leards range, PEI: a square wooden tower built in 1879 that is now a summer museum.

corrections.why: The PEI Lighthouse Society's technical data give a focal height of 11.3 m (37.0 ft); the record's 12.0 m comes from OpenStreetMap.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1873 is Rowlett's station-establishment date (the light on the pole and the new lantern of that year). The front tower is 1879 (PEI Lighthouse Society; LighthouseFriends), and the story uses 1879 for the tower.

LighthouseFriends and the Department's 1910 statement give 13 August 1901 for James Inman at the inner light; the Department's 1902 statement lists the inner light as vacant. The story states both and does not settle it.
PEI Society and LighthouseFriends: recognized under the PEI Heritage Places Protection Act on 3 October 2012; Rowlett gives a 2019 heritage designation. The story gives 2012 and notes Rowlett's 2019.

notes_for_editor: NAMING: the record's 'Leards Range Front' is the seaward light of the Victoria Harbour pair; LighthouseFriends and the PEI Society call it Leard's Front Range Light; the Marine reports call the harbour 'Crapaud'. The 'rear range' in the record (Victoria Range Light, close to the front) is probably the Palmer back range housed in the same tower (Rowlett: Palmer rear inactive since 2010; PEI Society: the tower housed the Palmer back range); the story does not treat it as a separate station. STATUS IS DISPUTED AND STATED IN THE STORY: PEI Lighthouse Society 'Active - Open', seasonal, night only; LighthouseFriends says the front light remains active as Victoria Harbour Lighthouse (undated page); Rowlett says inactive since 2011 and deactivated February 2020. The record's status 'active' is from OSM. A human should check the Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights. DATES: built 1879 (PEI Society and LighthouseFriends) vs 1878 'some documents'; first light 1873 (Rowlett) vs 1869 beacon (PEI Society and LighthouseFriends). The story uses 1869 for the beacon and 1879 for the tower. HERITAGE: 2012 (PEI Society, LighthouseFriends) vs 2019 (Rowlett); the story states both. LIGHT CHARACTERISTIC: the PEI Society gives flashing white (0.1 s flash, 3.9 s eclipse, night only, seasonal); the record says 'F R' (from OSM). Not used. HEIGHTS: front tower 10.7 m (PEI Society, LighthouseFriends) vs 10.5 m (Rowlett). Not stated in the story. Correction proposed for the focal height only. KEEPERS: the front and rear rosters are LighthouseFriends' own. Howatt's 22 July 1893 appointment and station line in the Department's statement for the year ended 30 June 1902 were checked on the page image (scan p. 246, printed p. 69). Inman's 13 August 1901 date was checked on the image of the statement for the year ended 30 June 1910 (scan p. 255, printed p. 253). The 1902 statement shows the Crapaud Inner Range Light as '(Vacant)', checked on the image (scan p. 246), which conflicts with LighthouseFriends' Inman date. Leard is 'Leard, Solomon J' in the statement for the year ended 30 June 1900 (scan p. 229); not matched to the station. Emerson Malcom MacDonald is on both lists (front 1940 to 1960; rear 1951 to 1960), kept as two lines. Kenneth C. Holm, Stewart Gordon Inman and Harry B. Clark have spelling variants in the PEI Society page. Donald W. Palmer's 1874 to 1875 dates are LighthouseFriends' and agree with the PEI Society's. OWNERSHIP: LighthouseFriends says the Coast Guard discontinued the range in 2011; the PEI Society and Rowlett say ownership passed to the Village of Victoria in 2012. STORMS AND WRECKS: no wreck or rescue tied to this light was found in the sources read; the only storm mentioned is the 1895 gale that damaged the rear-light mast and dwelling (LighthouseFriends). No newspaper search was run for this Canadian station. No photos added. The Victoria Seaport Museum's own site was not read; the PEI Society's page was used for hours.
